quote: Your stop-payment fee ($25 vs a $30 median) and two other lines sit below the market range.

findings.headline: Several lines are priced below the market.
findings.body: Your stop-payment fee ($25 vs a $30 median), cashier's check fee ($3 vs a $6 median) and incoming wire fee ($5 vs a $12.50 median) each sit below the peer 25th percentile. These are customer-favorable positions that peers' published schedules can verify.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 5 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, two sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles and three below.

findings.stat_label: not found in your published schedule
findings.headline: Some headline fees are not in the schedule we found.
findings.body: We did not find a monthly maintenance fee in your published documents, although 10 or more peers publish one. If you charge it, the amount may sit in a separate disclosure; customers comparing schedules online will not see it.

exec_narrative: First Bank is compared with 60 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Texas have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 5 rankable lines, two sit inside the middle half of the market and three below it (stop-payment fee, cashier's check fee and incoming wire fee). We would suggest one step: check that the monthly maintenance fee is published where customers can find it.

callouts.title: Stop-payment fee — $25
callouts.stat: Peer median $30 · middle half $29.75–$31.25 · 17th percentile · n=12
callouts.body: Published as “Stop Payment - all items.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $30 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Cashier's check fee — $3
callouts.stat: Peer median $6 · middle half $5–$7.50 · 0th percentile · n=11
callouts.body: Published as “Cashier's check.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $6 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Fees we could not find in your published schedule
callouts.stat: Monthly maintenance fee: published by 10 peers (median $8.75)
callouts.body: Absence here means the line was not in the documents listed in § 06, not that you do not charge it. Regulators and comparison sites increasingly expect the full consumer fee schedule to be posted in one place.

callouts.title: Lines with too few peers to rank
callouts.stat: Non-network ATM fee $1 (n=5, median $2.25) · Card replacement fee $5 (n=6, median $10)
callouts.body: Fewer than eight comparable peers publish these lines, so we show them without a percentile or a flag. Treat any comparison as directional.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing First Bank with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
